prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 1 "Filling valve (internal frost-burst fitting)": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 52 (80% range 38 to 79); revealed per pc: 48-55 (case 16)
- line 2 "Connection hose": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 30 (80% range 22 to 45); revealed per pc: 27-33 (case 16)
- line 3 "Senior installer hours": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per hr about 97 (80% range 69 to 131); revealed per hr: >=91 (case 16), so this line (3 hr) about 290 (208 to 393)
- line 5 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 7 of 16 earlier cases, t = 0 in 9; when indemnified t per pc about 77 (80% range 65 to 88); revealed per pc: >=60 (case 16), >=68 (case 18), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), 34-45 (case 23)

items.rationale: Sections 2.4.4 and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like renewal of the fractured valve. The matching reference supports €52 gross for one valve.
Section 7.1.9 covers connection elements that must be renewed with the fractured fitting. The matching reference supports €30 gross for one hose.
Sections 7.1.7(f) and 7.1.9 cover necessary labour on the internal fitting. Three hours at about €97 gross per hour gives approximately €290 for the line.

Sections 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.9 cover consumables actually used in the repair, but section 3.6(c) excludes the contractor's own small equipment. Allow €9 for a modest quantity of repair consumables if substantiated.
Sections 7.1.9 and 7.1.11 allow one attendance for the covered fitting repair. Use the €77 gross prior for the single attendance.

Sections 2.4.6 and 5.2.2 expressly cover imaging equipment used to locate the internal escape. Allow €50 for equipment use alone, with labour and attendance billed separately; the €2,500 gross leak-location cap does not bind.

Sections 2.6.4 and 3.5 exclude frost acting from outside because the optional peril is not shown as agreed. Section 2.4.3 does not apply because no escaped water reached the façade; €1 is a placeholder only.
Sections 3.5(b) and 5.2.1 exclude removal of plaster damaged solely by uninsured outdoor frost. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Sections 3.5(b) and 7.1.7 exclude base plaster work on the façade because its damage is not covered. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Sections 3.5(d) and 7.1.10 exclude the upgrade, and there is no like-for-like allowance because the underlying outdoor frost damage is also uninsured. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Section 3.5(b) excludes substrate reinstatement following uninsured outdoor frost damage. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Section 3.5(b) excludes the finish coats on the uninsured façade repair regardless of the number applied. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.6 exclude repainting separate undamaged elevations for visual uniformity. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Section 3.5(b) expressly excludes priming associated with uninsured outdoor frost repairs. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Sections 3.5(c) and 7.1.11 exclude all five hours because the labour relates to uninsured façade work. The €1 figure is a placeholder only.
Sections 3.5(c) and 7.1.12 exclude lump sums for uninsured façade work, and section 9.6 requires an identifiable covered purpose. None is shown; €1 is a placeholder only.
